agree.reason: The offer of invoices and a meeting before May 1, plus a concrete ask tied to the July 1 renewal, gives a skeptical director something to check rather than just another rate complaint, though the letter never shows her the size of the loss in dollars.

honest.reason: It drops the unsupported 'a third will close' claim and openly says the cause of the 9 closures is unknown, but 'often the only pharmacy' and 'done it for years' go a little beyond the facts, and 'a 40-mile round trip' understates the 'more than 20 miles' it comes from.

works_the_facts.reason: It never uses the 3,100 prescriptions at Reilly Drug and never turns the $1.80 gap into a yearly loss per pharmacy or across the 38, so the strongest numbers it could have built are left unused.

right_comparison.reason: It describes the alternative the facts support: a chain more than 20 miles away or mail order in 14 counties, against a background of 9 closures in two years and two pharmacies ready to stop serving plan members.

qualification.reason: The invoice offer and the May 1 meeting deadline are things the reader can check and are dated, but the letter never says what follows if the July 1 contract leaves rates below cost, beyond the two pharmacies' general threat.

objections.reason: It answers 'members have plenty of chains' with the 14 counties and the 20-mile distance, and answers 'they complain every year' with checkable invoices and the January start date, without raising objections the facts already settle.

fit.reason: It is a one-page open letter with a clear signature and contact line, and it works for both the plan and the newspapers.
